Revenue growth

Examining a company’s long-term performance can provide clues about its quality. Any business can deliver a good quarter or two, but many enduring ones grow for years. Over the last five years, MarketAxess grew its revenue at a sluggish 4.3% compounded annual growth rate. This was underwhelming for the financials sector and leaves the company with a poor growth baseline.

Long-term growth is the most important, but within financials, a half-decade historical view may miss recent interest rate changes and market returns. MarketAxess’s annualized revenue growth of 3.6% over the last two years aligns with its five-year trend, suggesting its demand was consistently weak.
Note: Quarters not shown were determined to be outliers because they were impacted by outsized investment gains/losses that are not indicative of the recurring fundamentals of the business.
This quarter, MarketAxess’s revenue of $210.4 million was flat year on year, falling short of Wall Street’s consensus estimates.
Key takeaways from MarketAxess’s Q3 results

MarketAxess had few positives to offer in a softer quarter, with both EBITDA and revenue falling short of Wall Street’s consensus estimates. Shares remained flat at $164.66 immediately after the release.
Is MarketAxess a buy? The latest quarter matters, but not nearly as much as longer-term fundamentals and valuation when deciding whether to buy the stock.
